problem: Given that the polynomial $f(x)={x}^{3}+{x}^{2}-14x-24$ has one of its roots in the interval $(3,8),$ find the sum of the distinct real roots of $f(x).$

feedback.problem: According to the rational roots theorem, which of the following **cannot** be a root of the polynomial $f(x)=2{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}-2x-1?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Given a polynomial with integer coefficients, the rational roots theorem states that any rational roots of the polynomial must take the form

$$
\pm \frac{\text{factor of the constant term}}{\text{factor of the leading coefficient}}.
$$

For the given polynomial $f(x),$ the constant term is $-1$ and the leading coefficient is $2.$ So, any rational roots of $f(x)$ must take the form

$$
\pm \frac{\text{factor of }-1}{\text{factor of }2}.
$$

Of the given answer choices, only $2$ does not take the above form. The value $2$ can be interpreted as a fraction $\frac{2}{1},$ and the numerator $(2)$ is not a factor of $-1.$
